output.reason: A 68-year-old with two weeks of worsening bilateral ankle swelling and now two nights of orthopnea requiring sitting up to breathe suggests decompensated heart failure needing immediate emergency assessment with oxygen saturation, chest imaging and cardiac evaluation.
output.patientMessage: Go to the emergency department now. Swelling in both ankles plus needing to sit up to breathe at night can mean fluid backing up from a heart or related problem, which needs same-hour tests that messaging cannot provide. Have someone drive you, or call 911 if breathing worsens, you get chest pain, or you feel faint.
differential: Decompensated heart failure with pulmonary congestion
Other cause of fluid overload (e.g. kidney or liver disease)
